title: Numbers, days and dates
topic: numbers from 0 to 1000; days, months, dates; age and prices
why: With the time (My day), you already handle numbers up to 12; this lesson takes them up to 1000. It gives you what you need right away in Spain: saying your age, understanding a price, giving a date, and telling el lunes (this Monday) from los lunes (every Monday).

Numbers from 0 to 99

You already know the numbers for telling the time. Here's the rest up to 30. From 16 to 29, the number is written as a single word: dieciséis = \"ten and six\", veintiuno = \"twenty and one\".

NumberSpanishNumberSpanish
0cero16dieciséis
11once17diecisiete
12doce18dieciocho
13trece19diecinueve
14catorce20veinte
15quince21veintiuno
22veintidós26veintiséis
23veintitrés27veintisiete
24veinticuatro28veintiocho
25veinticinco29veintinueve

Watch the accents: dieciséis, veintidós, veintitrés, veintiséis.

From 31 on: tens + y + units

30 treinta · 40 cuarenta · 50 cincuenta · 60 sesenta · 70 setenta · 80 ochenta · 90 noventa

After 30, you write three words, with y (and) in the middle: treinta y uno (31), cuarenta y cinco (45), noventa y nueve (99). Like English \"thirty-one\", it's simply tens then units, with \"and\" instead of the hyphen. No surprises after sixty: Spanish counts in tens, just like English.

Uno becomes un or una

Before a noun, uno becomes un (masculine) or una (feminine), even at the end of a bigger number:

Tengo veintiún años. Javier tiene treinta y un años.I'm twenty-one. Javier is thirty-one.
Somos veintiuna personas en clase.There are twenty-one of us in class.

With no noun after it, keep uno: —¿Cuántos años tiene? —Veintiuno. And in a date: el veintiuno de mayo.

From 100 to 1000, and prices

Cien = exactly 100, or 100 before a noun: cien euros. As soon as another number follows, say ciento: ciento uno (101), ciento veinte (120).

NumberSpanish
200doscientos
300trescientos
400cuatrocientos
500quinientos
600seiscientos
700setecientos
800ochocientos
900novecientos
1000mil
  • Three irregular forms: quinientos (not \"cincocientos\"), setecientos, novecientos.
  • Hundreds agree with a feminine noun: doscientos euros, but doscientas personas.
  • The y only goes between the tens and the units: trescientos cuarenta y cinco (345), never \"trescientos y cuarenta\", even though English says \"three hundred and forty-five\".
  • Mil takes no \"one\" (no \"a thousand\") and doesn't change: mil euros, dos mil.

Prices

To ask a price, you use two set phrases. The verb agrees with whatever costs money:

One thingSeveral things
¿Cuánto cuesta el libro?¿Cuánto cuestan los zapatos?
Cuesta quince euros.Cuestan noventa euros.

As in English, euro takes an -s in the plural: un euro, dos euros. For cents: tres euros con cincuenta (céntimos) or simply tres cincuenta.

To react to a price: ¡Es caro! (it's expensive!) or ¡Es barato! (it's cheap!). The trap: saying \"cuánto cuesta los zapatos\". Look at the noun: plural, so cuestan.

", "

Days, months and dates

SpanishEnglish
lunesMonday
martesTuesday
miércolesWednesday
juevesThursday
viernesFriday
sábadoSaturday
domingoSunday

Unlike English, days are written with a lowercase letter, and they're masculine. From Monday to Friday, the plural doesn't change: el lunes, los lunes; but el sábado → los sábados, el domingo → los domingos.

El lunes or los lunes?

SpanishMeaning
El lunes trabajo en casa.On Monday (this one Monday).
Los lunes trabajo en casa.On Mondays (every Monday).
Los domingos como con la familia.On Sundays (every Sunday).

Where English uses \"on\", Spanish always puts an article before the day (except after es: Hoy es martes). So \"On Monday I work\" is El lunes trabajo, never \"en lunes trabajo\" or \"lunes trabajo\".

Months and the date

enero, febrero, marzo, abril, mayo, junio, julio, agosto, septiembre, octubre, noviembre, diciembre: lowercase too, unlike English.

The date is el + number + de + month, like \"the third of May\": el tres de mayo, el veinte de julio. No ordinals (\"third\") except for the 1st, which can be el uno or el primero.

—¿Qué día es hoy? —Hoy es jueves, el siete de mayo de dos mil veintiséis.—What's the date today? —Today is Thursday, May 7th, 2026.
—¿Cuándo es el cumpleaños de Ana? —Es el catorce de julio.—When is Ana's birthday? —It's July 14th.

Age uses tener, and cuántos agrees with años: ¿Cuántos años tienes? —Tengo cuarenta y dos años.
